cause: The floating node panel still used a wide text Actions button, the drag-node affordance was stretched by the shared button minimum height, and native CSS resize exposed only a bottom-right handle. A focused RED test reproduced the missing compact-control and four-corner contracts before implementation.

evidence.ref: Focused regression and full frontend Vitest passed: 188 files and 1634 tests. Typecheck and git diff --check passed. Browser acceptance measured 27x27px Node actions and Drag node panel controls, 16x16px hitboxes for top-left/top-right/bottom-left/bottom-right, and used real pointer drags on all four corners. Each corner changed width and height; top corners moved the top edge and left corners moved the left edge. The floating panel was restored to x=36, y=116, width=680, height=572. The integrated quick gate's backend stage reported 4584 passed, 35 failed, 5 skipped, and 1 xfailed; failures were sandbox-exec permission failures and existing golden snapshot drift, unrelated to these frontend paths.

impact: Floating node chrome now uses the same compact square control footprint as the shared window controls, with a visible compact Actions glyph and stronger drag-handle dots. Users can resize the floating node panel from any corner while preserving minimum dimensions and corner-specific anchoring. The repository-wide quick gate remains red only for pre-existing macOS sandbox-exec and golden-snapshot failures outside this UI change.
lesson: When replacing browser-native resize with controlled corner handles, test both hitbox presence and directional geometry with real pointer drags, then restore the persisted panel position and size before handoff. Keep repository-wide environment failures separate from feature-specific acceptance evidence.
